name: Placentubex

image.caption: Placentubex Dramatically Smooths Your Skin, Reduces Wrinkles 1976

lead: Placentubex was a placenta-extract skin cream presented by Friedrich Merz at an international beauty care conference in 1953 as an anti-wrinkle moisturiser. Merz's own history describes it as a turning point for cosmetics [1].
It is relevant to looks as an early example of a cream marketed to soften the appearance of wrinkles, a category that later grew into modern anti-ageing skincare.

paras: The product was a topical cream applied to the skin as a moisturiser. No usage details from current sources are available.
No current safety data on this specific product is available. Placenta extract is an animal-derived ingredient used in various skincare products.

angle.text: The cream was positioned as a moisturiser that improves the look of wrinkles. People interested in it today usually encounter it as skincare history.

lead: Placentubex was an anti-wrinkle moisturising cream containing placenta extract, presented by Friedrich Merz in 1953 at an international beauty care conference and described by the company as marking a turning point in cosmetics [1].

A US patent granted in 1962 (filed 1959) describes a skin-care composition built on a steroid-hormone-free, albumin-containing extract of animal placenta or ovaries, with the stated purpose of reducing folds and wrinkles and giving a more youthful look [2]. Placenta-extract creams of this type are the category in which Placentubex belongs.

paras: Merz says Friedrich Merz presented Placentubex in 1953 as a moisturising cream for wrinkles [1]. A related US patent describes a steroid-hormone-free skin composition prepared from animal placenta or ovary extract [2].
A US patent granted in 1962 describes a similar composition, a steroid-hormone-free extract of animal placenta or ovary, usually from pigs, mixed into emulsions or lotions to reduce wrinkles [2].
No studies found on Placentubex itself.
